source: The implementation of the operationalization of the proposed adjustment is contingent upon the completion of the facilitation of the team's alignment process.
expectedBehavior: Flag genuinely opaque, indirect meaning. Prefer a precise local explanation, not wholesale prose generation.

source: The team will publish the report on Friday. Please send corrections by Thursday afternoon.
expectedBehavior: Clear instructions should not be flagged merely to produce findings.

source: Although the first experiment failed because the sensor was damaged, the second experiment used a replacement sensor and produced consistent measurements across all three trials.
expectedBehavior: Length alone is not a clarity problem; the causal relationships here are explicit.

source: I emailed Miriam about Sofia after she missed the deadline.
expectedBehavior: The reader cannot identify whether Miriam or Sofia missed the deadline.

source:
The server rejected requests without an authentication token.

This policy prevented anonymous access to private documents.
expectedBehavior: Use neighboring context; this policy has a clear antecedent.

source: Miriam asked Sofia to revise the report. Sofia will send the revision tomorrow.
expectedBehavior: Explicit names avoid reference ambiguity; return no finding.

source:
The survey found no meaningful difference in completion time between the two groups.

The survey results indicate that the groups did not differ meaningfully in how long they took to finish.

We therefore compared their error rates instead.
expectedBehavior: Flag the second paragraph's unnecessary restatement of the first result, not the distinct next step.

source:
The first group finished in ten minutes.

The second group finished in twelve minutes but made fewer errors.
expectedBehavior: Distinct comparison results are not redundant merely because vocabulary is shared.

source:
Please submit the signed form by Friday.

You can upload the form through the secure portal or bring it to reception.

As a reminder, Friday is the deadline because payroll closes that evening.
expectedBehavior: A short, useful closing reminder with its reason is not automatically a problem.

source:
This report compares the two options on cost, reliability, and deployment time.

Option A costs $10,000, while Option B costs $12,000.

These cost figures establish Option A as the less expensive choice, and conclude our comparison.
expectedBehavior: Flag the missing reliability/deployment discussion promised in the opening. Cross-paragraph reorganization should be report-only.

source:
We compared the two options on cost and deployment time.

Option A costs $10,000 and takes two weeks to deploy. Option B costs $12,000 and takes one week.

Choose Option A if cost matters most, or Option B if deployment speed matters most.
expectedBehavior: The comparison fulfills its opening promise and reaches a supported recommendation.

source:
Please approve the attached budget by Thursday.

The revised total is $5,000 lower than the previous estimate because we removed the optional workshop.

Reply with your approval or any requested changes, and I will send the final version to finance.
expectedBehavior: A clear action, relevant context and explicit next step need no formulaic restructuring.

source:
I spent two years abroad and I did not know what I wanted to dedicate the rest of my life to.

That was until I took my first physics class. It showed me how much I enjoy understanding how things work.
expectedBehavior: The second paragraph's reference resolves against the first; a clear cross-paragraph transition must not be flagged for a supposedly missing prior state.

source: I have always been a creative and hard-working person who loves learning. My experiences have shaped me into the person I am today. I am confident that my background makes me a strong candidate.
expectedBehavior: Flag the generic, unsupported claims as a development opportunity, with guidance or a question rather than invented specifics, praise, or a prescribed outline.
expectedQuote: shaped me into the person I am today

source: During the two-year program I kept a 3.8 GPA while working twenty hours a week as a lab technician. When the lab's calibration routine started producing inconsistent readings, I rebuilt the spreadsheet that tracked sensor drift, and the error rate dropped from four percent to under one.
expectedBehavior: Concrete, supported claims with a verifiable result should not be flagged as underdeveloped or in need of more examples.

source:
Set the threshold to the drift value from step 2 and restart the collector.

The collector then reports anomalies every minute to the log service.
expectedBehavior: In technical writing, flag the undefined prerequisite (the drift value from an absent step 2) as a reader-facing problem, without rewriting the whole procedure.

source: The categorization of the nonconformances was performed by the review committee prior to the initiation of the remediation planning.
expectedBehavior: Flag the stacked nominalizations that hide who does what. Explain the specific reading problem instead of replacing the whole sentence.

source: Regarding the attached contract, there is an issue with the section about termination that we may want to look at possibly.
expectedBehavior: The reader cannot tell what is being asked or by when. Ask for the missing decision or action rather than drafting a new email.
expectedQuote: may want to look at possibly

source:
Open the collector settings and set the sampling interval to 250 milliseconds.

Save the change and restart the collector.

The next log entry confirms the new interval.
expectedBehavior: A short ordered procedure with explicit actions and a verification step is already clear.

source: Marco told Daniel that his proposal was approved, but he was not sure whether the budget committee had seen it yet.
expectedBehavior: At least one pronoun has two plausible people as its antecedent. Name the person instead of guessing.

source: Priya asked Lena to resend the contract because her signature page was missing.
expectedBehavior: It is unclear whose signature page is missing. Prefer a focused question or guidance naming the ambiguity.

source:
The collector and the log service both write to the same directory.

The collector retries for thirty seconds; the log service does not.
expectedBehavior: Each sentence names its own system, so the reference is unambiguous.

source:
Only 12 percent of participants completed the follow-up survey.

The follow-up survey was completed by only 12 percent of the participants.

This limits how far the result can be generalized.
expectedBehavior: Flag the second paragraph as a restatement of the first result. The distinct limitation in the third paragraph is not redundant.

source:
The sample was small, so the result should be treated as preliminary.

Because the sample was small, the finding is preliminary and should not be overinterpreted.
expectedBehavior: Two consecutive paragraphs carry the same caveat. Report the duplication; do not merge the author's paragraphs automatically.

source:
Please review the attached agenda before Monday.

If you want to add an item, send it to me by Sunday evening.

The final agenda will be distributed on Monday morning.
expectedBehavior: Each paragraph adds a distinct step or deadline, so shared vocabulary is not redundancy.

source:
This section explains how to install the collector, configure its filters, and verify the log output.

Download the installer and run it with default options.

The collector then starts automatically at every boot.
expectedBehavior: The opening promises filter configuration and log verification that the section never delivers. Report the gap; do not write the missing steps.
expectedQuote: configure its filters, and verify the log output

source:
Three factors shaped the decision.

The first factor was cost.

The second factor was the timeline.
expectedBehavior: The announced structure is incomplete. Flag the missing third factor as a structural gap rather than inventing it.

source:
I started with a failed prototype.

The second prototype fixed the sensor mount but introduced a wiring fault.

The third version passed all three bench tests, which is why the design was approved.
expectedBehavior: A three-step narrative that delivers what its opening sets up needs no restructuring.

source:
This essay evaluates the relocation proposal on cost, staff continuity, and access to public transport.

The relocation would cost $180,000 in the first year, against $120,000 for staying put.

Lease terms are fixed for seven years, so the cost comparison assumes no renegotiation before then.

Two of the four team leads said they would not move to the suburban site.

The new building has parking for forty cars and a bus stop two blocks away.

Overall, the proposal looks attractive on financial grounds and should be approved.
expectedBehavior: Across the whole document, staff continuity is raised but never evaluated, and the conclusion claims more than the paragraphs support. Report the cross-paragraph gap without reorganizing or rewriting the essay.
expectedQuote: cost, staff continuity, and access to public transport

source: I am a natural leader with excellent communication skills and strong technical ability. These qualities make me an ideal fit for the role.
expectedBehavior: Flag the unsupported self-assessment as a development opportunity, with guidance or a question that invites the author's own evidence. Never invent examples or praise.
expectedQuote: natural leader with excellent communication skills

source: The new routine is significantly faster and more reliable than the previous one.
expectedBehavior: A comparative claim with no measurement is underdeveloped. Ask for the numbers the author actually observed instead of supplying them.

source: My first prototype failed because I soldered the sensor directly to the board. Re-reading the bench log showed the joint had cracked under vibration, so the second prototype used a strain relief loop and passed all three tests.
expectedBehavior: Specific cause, evidence and outcome are already developed; adding generic advice would be noise.

source:
Calibrate the sensor before the first run.

Connect the collector, start the log service, and open the calibration panel.

Set the threshold to the drift value recorded during calibration and confirm that the panel shows the new value.

Run the collector for ten minutes and export the log.

If anomalies appear, repeat the calibration with a lower threshold.
expectedBehavior: In technical writing, flag the missing prerequisite detail (what the recorded drift value is and where it is stored) as a reader-facing gap without rewriting the whole procedure.
expectedQuote: the drift value recorded during calibration

source: Honestly, this whole thing is a total mess and nobody really knows what to do about it.
expectedBehavior: The custom reviewer reports only what its own instructions define. It should flag the vague, unsupported characterization without rewriting the paragraph in its own voice.

source: The bench test recorded 14 successful cycles and one failed cycle at 60 degrees Celsius.
expectedBehavior: A concrete factual statement with numbers is not a finding for this reviewer.

source:
The migration was difficult and everyone agreed it went badly.

The first two attempts failed because the export tool could not handle files larger than 2 GB.

The third attempt split the archive into 1 GB parts and completed in 40 minutes.

The team's overall impression was that the new process is much better, although no measurements were recorded.
expectedBehavior: Across multiple paragraphs, flag the unsupported overall judgement while leaving the specific, evidenced paragraphs alone.
expectedQuote: the new process is much better

source:
This report evaluates the proposed archive consolidation on retrieval speed, storage cost, and audit traceability.

The current setup keeps three regional copies, each indexed separately, and a request is answered by whichever regional index resolves first.

Consolidation would replace the three indexes with one global index and keep the regional copies as cold storage.

Retrieval is the clearest benefit: a cross-region query today has to query all three indexes and merge the results, which adds an average of 900 milliseconds.

Storage cost is where the proposal is weakest. The cold copies still count against the quarterly storage budget, so consolidation saves indexing cost but not the dominant storage line item.

The finance review estimated a 6 percent reduction in indexing spend and no change in total storage spend.

Audit traceability is discussed only in one sentence: the proposal states that a single index would make audits simpler.

No audit workflow is described, no retention rule is compared between the regional and global index, and the report never says who signs off on audit readiness.

The recommendation is to consolidate in the next planning cycle because the retrieval improvement is meaningful and the risk is described as low.
expectedBehavior: Across a long document, flag the promised audit-traceability evaluation that is never delivered, and the conclusion's unsupported risk claim. Report the gap only; do not reorganize or rewrite the report.
expectedQuote: retrieval speed, storage cost, and audit traceability

source:
The migration team measured a 40 percent reduction in export time after switching to the streaming exporter.

The streaming exporter reduced export time by 40 percent, which the team took as confirmation that the old exporter was the bottleneck.

The first benchmark ran on a 12 GB archive; the second ran on a 14 GB archive after the streaming exporter was enabled.

Because the two benchmarks used different archive sizes, the 40 percent figure was recalculated against the same archive and reported again as a 40 percent improvement.

The team also noted that the streaming exporter writes to the same temporary directory as the old exporter.

That shared temporary directory is a real operational risk, and it is the only new risk the report identifies.
expectedBehavior: Flag the restated benchmark result and the recalculated duplicate of the same 40 percent figure. The distinct operational risk in the final paragraph must not be reported as redundant.
